title: An Interview With Roblox CEO David Baszucki About Aggregating Play
text: An Interview With Roblox CEO David Baszucki About Aggregating Play – Stratechery by Ben Thompson Skip to content By Ben Thompson About Email/RSS @benthompson Explore Concepts Companies Topics Menu Search × Stratechery Plus Subscribe Log In Learn More Member Forum By Ben Thompson About Email/RSS @benthompson Explore Concepts Companies Topics More by Ben Thompson Updates Interviews Year in Review All Articles Latest Podcast Jensen Huang Likely Out at Nvidia; The Megaspeed Maelstrom in D.C.; APEC in Seven Days; Legislation That May Come Next Sharp China | Nov 11 Jensen Huang Likely Out at Nvidia; The Megaspeed Maelstrom in D.C.; APEC in Seven Days; Legislation That May Come Next An Interview With Roblox CEO David Baszucki About Aggregating Play Thursday, November 12, 2026 Listen to Podcast Listen to this post: Good morning, This week’s Stratechery Interview is with Roblox CEO David Baszucki . I’ve interviewed Baszucki twice, in February 2022 , and November 2023 . What struck me about this interview is just how much AI has changed the landscape for Roblox. This was a company predicated on the concept that anyone can make a game, but now, for the first time, literally anyone can make a game. That means a world of abundance, and in that world, there is an opportunity to be an Aggregator, and Roblox is aggressively pursuing that opportunity. To that end, we discuss how AI has changed Baszucki’s view of what is possible, what goes into a game creation harness, making games on your phone, and the power of recommendation. Then we talk about Roblox’s vision of a universal player, where a Roblox game works everywhere, and Roblox Everywhere, where Roblox developers can use the platform beyond the Roblox app. We also touch on advertising — the natural Aggregator business model — and whether Baszucki still thinks he is building the metaverse. As a reminder, all Stratechery content, including interviews, is available as a podcast; click the link at the top of this email to add Stratechery to your podcast player. On to the Interview: An Interview With Roblox CEO David Baszucki About Aggregating Play This interview is lightly edited for clarity. Topics: The AI Impact | A Game Creation Harness | Roblox Build | Roblox Discovery | Universal Player | Roblox Everywhere | Advertising | Metaverses The AI Impact David Baszucki, welcome back to Stratechery. DB: Thank you, Ben, for having me back. It’s great to be here. So this is the third time I’ve interviewed you, and I want to sort of put that in an interesting context. First, you started Roblox in 2004, you went public in 2021, you first talked to me in 2022 and again in 2023 , that’s like a nearly 20-year stretch. Now it’s 2026, and here’s my question: Is the world more different for you now, compared to three years before, than it was for the entire first two decades from starting the company to the last time we talked? DB: The changes in the world we all feel are sure happening a lot more rapidly. When we first published Roblox — I don’t know if people on this podcast remember — software used to be distributed on floppy disks and CDs. You know, the funny thing is, you’re the second person I’ve interviewed in the last two or three weeks where we’ve referenced back to fact that the reason we say packaged software is it used to actually be packaged! DB: It’s been crazy, we had the Internet, when we started the company, we had the vision of a category called immersive co-experience, sci-fi writers have been writing about the holodeck forever, and we went along our way. I’m still pro-metaverse, we can use the word metaverse, it’s okay. DB: Okay, good, we use them all. It’s Snow Crash — metaverse, holodeck, they’re all good. We started on this vision of building human co-experience, we saw the mobile age come across us, we saw the crypto age. The AI acceleration wave we’re in is faster and bigger and crazier than anything I’ve ever seen, it’s changing how we think about the product, it’s changing how people are going to create games. What’s really exciting is, when we started the company, we had this slogan called “You Make the Game”. Yep. DB: We started with that slogan, we learned along the way that the ratio of people who might want to play games to make games has drifted — more people want to just play games than make games, because historically making games has been Roblox Studio and 3D editing and writing script. We could be approaching the time where “You Make the Game” really comes true, and where making a game is accessible to everyone. It’s really fun, I’ll tell you a bit about some of the experiments we’ve been having with Roblox Build . But we’re entering an era where making a game could be as big as playing a game. I’m right there with you. We’re obviously going to touch on all those points, I think it’s probably predictable what we want to talk about. But to go back to 2023, you called AI then, “a super paintbrush and a super 3D modeler, rather than a full replacement” — Is that still how you’re thinking about AI? DB: It’s what the data is proving out. We just had our earnings call a few weeks ago , we highlighted a lot of acceleration. One, there’s various ways humans can augment with AI on Roblox, they can use MCP , which is like plugging in a model, they can use the Roblox AI assistant to help build. And what do you mean with that MCP server? You mentioned you had 5x growth quarter-over-quarter. That’s where you’re actually using Claude Code or Codex or whatever to work with Roblox? DB: People are plugging in, we can see all of them — Claude Code, Codex, other models — all being plugged into Roblox Studio to help build things.
